task.name: Routing excludes unavailable models and stops a phase before spend when no model remains
task.story_text:
---
depends_on:
  - issue-2949
---

## What

Slice 2 of 3 from the decomposition of #2914. Consumes the availability answers defined in #2949 and threads them into assignment and preflight: unavailable models are excluded from every candidate pool with a logged reason, unverified ones stay eligible with a one-time warning, and a phase left with nothing available or unverified stops the run before any spend. Post-dispatch quarantine is the third slice, not this one.

## Why

Knowing a model is unavailable is worthless unless the router acts on it before the money goes. In the 2026-09-04 incident the refusal arrived after WORKSPACE, preflight, routing and plan had been charged; four stories produced nothing. The availability answer now exists (#2949); this slice is where it changes what gets dispatched. See #2914.

## Acceptance criteria

- A model resolved **unavailable** appears in no phase's candidate pool. Its exclusion is recorded in the routing decision with a canonical reason naming the auth mode and the time of the availability answer, in the same place and shape other exclusions (self-review, taint) are recorded today.
- A model resolved **unverified** remains fully eligible, and the run warns exactly once per model that its availability is unconfirmed. Routing among unverified models is identical to routing today; nothing degrades for a provider that publishes no catalog.
- A phase left with no available or unverified model stops the run before any spend on that story, naming every excluded model and its reason. The stop is a routing outcome, not an agent failure, and is never recorded against any model's capability history.
- Exclusion is applied at the moment of selection from the current availability answer, so an answer that changes between stories in one sprint changes routing for later stories without a restart.

## Example

```
$ forge sprint --issues 2775 ...
  ⚠ ROUTING  openai/gpt-5.4/cli excluded — not available to this account under
             codex ChatGPT-account auth (account catalog, checked 2026-09-05)
  ▸ DEV   gpt-5.4-mini  iter=1
  ✓ DEV   $0.42  4m 11s
```

And where nothing remains:

```
  ✗ ROUTING  no model available for phase dev: openai/gpt-5.4/cli excluded
             (not available to this account), openai/gpt-5.5/cli excluded
             (not available to this account). Nothing dispatched, $0.00 spent.
```

handoff.summary: Threaded the #2949 availability answer into routing as a pure input, mirroring the capability-record pattern. New src/theforge/model_availability.py owns target construction (moved out of cli/check_config.py so the diagnostic and the router resolve the same dispatch identity), per-selection resolution keyed on AgentDef.name, the canonical exclusion detail, and a warn-once tracker. assignment.py adds REASON_MODEL_UNAVAILABLE to EXCLUSION_REASONS, applies the exclusion to every role pool before any selection runs (so first pick, tier fallback, exploration, explicit pins and the budget enforcer all draw from the filtered pool), renders it in all five candidate pools with the auth mode/checked_at/freshness/reason detail, and raises the new NoAvailableModelError when a phase empties. A new sprint/availability_gate.py runs beside the auth gate — tier-independent, whole-pool, pins honored via a shared explicit_role_overrides() extracted from _apply_preflight_config — so a phase with no invocable model stops the launch ahead of intake remediation, batch preflight and every dispatch. The refusal is caught at all three _apply_preflight_config call sites (live preflight_flow plus the cached and resume paths in engine.py) and returned as an infrastructure-flagged CoordinatorResult with error_type RoutingStopped: the existing 'this run made no statement about the story' contract, which is what keeps the stop out of capability history and model profiles. Availability is resolved fresh inside _apply_preflight_config (no signature change, so every caller gets it) and again at the post-plan checkpoint, so an answer that changes mid-sprint changes routing for later stories without a restart. forge explain renders the new reason from its detail; runbook and adaptive-assignment docs updated.

commits.message: feat(routing): exclude unavailable models and stop a phase before spend

acceptance_criteria.criterion: A model resolved unavailable appears in no phase's candidate pool. Its exclusion is recorded in the routing decision with a canonical reason naming the auth mode and the time of the availability answer, in the same place and shape other exclusions (self-review, taint) are recorded today.
acceptance_criteria.notes: REASON_MODEL_UNAVAILABLE joins EXCLUSION_REASONS; _availability_pool_entry marks the entry in both _single_model_pool and _reviewer_candidate_pool (checked first, so the reason is never buried under a tier mismatch), with detail {state, auth_mode, checked_at, freshness, reason}. role_pools are filtered before any selection, so no fallback path can reseat one. Tested per role plus exact detail fields.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: A model resolved unverified remains fully eligible, and the run warns exactly once per model that its availability is unconfirmed. Routing among unverified models is identical to routing today; nothing degrades for a provider that publishes no catalog.
acceptance_criteria.notes: Only MODEL_AVAILABILITY_UNAVAILABLE excludes. A parity test asserts an all-unverified decision equals the no-answer baseline across every seated model and every candidate_pool. AvailabilityWarnings keys on (name, state) so repeated stories stay quiet but a model whose answer later changes is announced again. A resolver failure yields no answers at all, i.e. fully eligible.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: A phase left with no available or unverified model stops the run before any spend on that story, naming every excluded model and its reason. The stop is a routing outcome, not an agent failure, and is never recorded against any model's capability history.
acceptance_criteria.notes: Two layers. The sprint gate is whole-pool and tier-independent, runs before intake remediation/batch preflight/any worktree touch, names every excluded model with its reason and states '$0.00 spent' — genuinely zero spend, no story marked failed. assign_models raises NoAvailableModelError for the exact per-phase case; the coordinator converts it to an infrastructure-flagged result (error_type RoutingStopped) with no model_profiles/model_capabilities write, asserted by a seam test. PARTIAL because a pool that only empties after tier narrowing is caught at assignment time, which on the live path is after that story's preflight was charged — see deferred_items.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Exclusion is applied at the moment of selection from the current availability answer, so an answer that changes between stories in one sprint changes routing for later stories without a restart.
acceptance_criteria.notes: resolve_agent_availability is called inside _apply_preflight_config (not at sprint startup, and not via a new parameter, so engine.py's cached and resume call sites resolve fresh too) and again in plan_flow before apply_post_plan_checkpoint. Seam test drives two consecutive _apply_preflight_config calls with a resolver whose answers differ and asserts the resolver was consulted twice and the dev candidate_pool reason changed.

story_deviations: An explicit operator pin resolved unavailable is REFUSED rather than honored-with-a-warning, which is how the capability gate treats pins. Rationale: a capability record is inferred evidence about behaviour, whereas the account catalog saying the credential cannot invoke the model means the dispatch cannot succeed — honoring the pin would spend the story's budget to discover that, and AC 3 says a phase with nothing available stops. Reads against ADR-0006 clause 1 operator sovereignty, so calling it out explicitly.

Extracted explicit_role_overrides() out of _apply_preflight_config into a module-level helper in coordinator/preflight.py. Not in the plan, but the sprint gate must ask the same 'which roles are pinned' question the router asks, and a second derivation would drift. Behaviour-preserving except that both pool guards now materialize the tuple before testing emptiness — the previous form asked 'is it non-empty' and 'what is in it' as two separate reads of a computed property, which IndexError'd the first time the gate called it on a test config.

Preflight's candidate_pool now receives capability_excluded like the other roles. No behavioural change (preflight is absent from ROLE_REQUIRED_CAPABILITY, so the map is always empty for it); done so the omission is a policy statement rather than a call site that forgot.
deferred_items: Residual pre-spend gap: the launch gate answers the whole-pool question, but a phase whose pool only empties after tier narrowing (e.g. tier-pinned profiles, or exploration restricting the pool) is refused by assign_models, which on the live coordinator path runs after that story's preflight has been charged. The plan reviewers flagged this; closing it needs exact per-phase tier pools to be derivable before the paid preflight produces the complexity score, which is a routing-sequence change beyond this slice. The cached-preflight and resume paths do refuse at $0.00 for that story.
Post-dispatch quarantine of a model that turns out to be unavailable at dispatch time is the third slice of #2914, deliberately not in scope here.

reviews.summary: [openai-gpt-5.5-cli] The main routing path is present, but unavailable models can still be dispatched through explicit multi-reviewer pools and the sprint gate can miss fully unavailable duplicate-model pools. | [anthropic-fable-cli] Solid, well-tested slice — unavailable models are excluded from every pool, unverified routes identically with warn-once, and mid-sprint answer changes reroute — but AC3 is not fully met on the live coordinator path: a story whose pool empties at assignment time has already been charged for preflight (agent invoked at preflight_flow.py:534, routing applied at :1140), yet the stop message hard-codes 'Nothing dispatched, $0.00 spent', which is false on that path. The dev handoff itself marks this criterion PARTIAL; gate verdict for HEAD is PASS. | [openai-gpt-5.6-sol-cli] The current PASS gate is authoritative, but multiple production paths still dispatch unavailable models, spend before stopping, suppress required warnings, or record routing stops as story failures.

findings.description: When an explicit review_pool or plan_agent_review pool has an available first reviewer and an unavailable later reviewer, the later unavailable reviewer is spliced back into the runtime reviewer list and the reconciled routing decision marks it included.
When two candidates in the same phase share the same model string and both catalog answers are unavailable, check_sprint_availability collapses them to one excluded entry and returns no stop.
After one run warns that a model is unverified, a later run in the same Python process using the same model and state emits no unverified warning.

On the live coordinator path the preflight agent runs and is charged (preflight_flow.py:534) before availability is resolved and routing is applied (preflight_flow.py:1140), so a NoAvailableModelError raised there stops the story after preflight spend while its operator-facing message asserts 'Nothing dispatched, $0.00 spent'.

When a role pool empties from the combination of capability exclusions and availability exclusions, the whole-pool guard raises NoAvailableModelError naming only the availability-excluded agents, so the stop message can attribute the emptiness entirely to account availability while capability records removed the other candidates.

check_sprint_availability keys its excluded map by model name while phase_keys is per profile, so a phase whose candidate list contains two profiles with the same model name never satisfies len(excluded) == len(phase_keys) and the launch gate silently passes even when every candidate is unavailable, deferring the stop to the router.

AVAILABILITY_WARNINGS is a process-wide singleton with a reset() method that no production code calls, so in a process that runs more than one sprint the 'once per run' warning is actually once per process and a later sprint's unverified models are silently unannounced.

When availability changes after sprint launch and leaves a later story unroutable, the story invokes and records its cost-bearing preflight agent before reading the fresh availability answer, so the reported $0.00 routing stop can occur after spend.
A per-story RoutingStopped result is classified as FAILED and does not set the sprint stop condition, so the routing outcome marks the story failed while independent stories remain schedulable.

When an explicit review or plan-review pool has an available first member and an unavailable later member, the later member is restored into the runtime reviewer list and candidate audit as included and can be dispatched.
With assignment disabled, story configuration returns before availability resolution, so static runs emit no unverified warning and ignore model-access changes after sprint launch.
In the daemon, a model warned as unverified during one sprint is suppressed in every later sprint in the same process because warning state is process-global and never reset.

When the post-plan availability answer marks the already-seated dev model unavailable, checkpoint bypasses or the absence of a reduced-tier replacement preserve that model for the subsequent DEV dispatch.
When two distinct candidate identities share the same model string and both are unavailable, the launch gate collapses them into one exclusion entry and fails to stop the sprint.
When availability excludes one candidate and a capability rule excludes the other, the empty-pool refusal names only the availability-excluded candidate and omits the other model and its reason.

plan_review.findings:
- [P1-impl] [openai-gpt-5.6-sol-cli] The plan's first stated risk is carried on an acceptance-critical surface. _apply_preflight_config() derives tier-specific planner/dev/reviewer pools only after paid preflight, while sprint/runner.py can spend on _run_intake_remediation_pass() before run_batch_preflight(). Step 4 promises only an 'earliest possible' precheck followed by exact enforcement after assignment, which explicitly permits preflight or intake spend before discovering that the actual phase pool is empty. The generic zero-spend test in Step 7 does not enumerate tier-dependent exhaustion or intake-remediation spend.
  Suggestion: Specify a pre-spend viability design that runs before intake remediation and batch preflight and can soundly determine every phase pool that the story may select, or revise the routing sequence so exact phase selection is available before the first paid call. Add seam tests for tier-specific exhaustion and intake auto-fix enabled, both asserting $0.00.
- [P1-impl] [openai-gpt-5.6-sol-cli] Steps 4 and 5 do not account for all callers of _apply_preflight_config(). Besides coordinator/preflight_flow.py, it is called directly from coordinator/engine.py on cache-valid fresh and resume paths. Sprint execution normally obtains batch-preflight state through sprint/collision.py::run_batch_preflight() and later enters those cached paths. Without updating engine.py, a new routing-refusal exception can escape as a generic failure, and later stories can reuse routing resolved during the upfront batch rather than resolving current availability at their actual selection boundary.
  Suggestion: Add src/theforge/coordinator/engine.py and the cached/resume call paths explicitly to Steps 4 and 5. Define how each caller receives a fresh answer and converts pool exhaustion into the same non-failure routing outcome; test both standalone and sprint cached-preflight execution.
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-opus-cli] Risk 1 (spend ordering) is retired only partially. Step 4 says catch the refusal 'at the coordinator routing boundary and at sprint pre-dispatch where possible' — but by the time assign_models runs, preflight complexity has already been paid, so a refusal raised only there would violate the AC's 'before any spend on that story'. Step 7 asserts zero spend but the plan does not state where the tier-independent precheck lives.
  Suggestion: Make the pre-dispatch precheck role-pool-wide and tier-independent: before any paid phase, resolve availability for every configured candidate of each required role and refuse if a role's whole pool is unavailable. Keep the assignment-time refusal as the exact per-phase enforcement, and have the Step 7 zero-spend test drive the sprint from before preflight, not from assign_models.
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-opus-cli] Risk 2 (account/auth-mode-scoped availability vs identity-scoped capability exclusions) is retired in shape but the key mapping is unspecified. resolve_model_availability keys its result dict on target.key or target.canonical_id (config/auth.py:~567), while candidate pools and capability_excluded are keyed on AgentDef.name (assignment.py:2101, 2189).
  Suggestion: Fix one explicit key convention in Step 1 (e.g. build targets with key=agent.name for assignment-facing resolution) and assert the mapping in the Step 7 seam test so a same-model-different-credentials pair does not collide or silently miss its exclusion.
- [P2] [anthropic-opus-cli] Step 5's per-story resolution can trigger a live account-catalog fetch (_openai_catalog) on every story; the resolver only memoizes catalogs within a single call, so failure/latency behavior across stories is unspecified.
  Suggestion: State that a catalog fetch failure yields unverified (fully eligible, warn once) rather than unavailable, and consider a short-lived per-sprint cache keyed on the dispatch identity tuple that still allows a changed answer to take effect for later stories.
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-fable-cli] Plan risk 1 (preflight complexity is itself paid spend) is retired for the whole-phase-empty case by the Step 4 pre-dispatch precheck and Step 7's zero-spend test, but one residual is unaddressed: if tier/exploration selection after paid preflight narrows the pool in a way that only then empties it (e.g. tier-pinned profiles), some preflight spend precedes the stop. The AC reads 'before any spend on that story'.
  Suggestion: Have the pre-dispatch precheck evaluate the union of all tiers' configured candidates per phase — if every configured identity for a phase is unavailable, stop before preflight dispatch; assignment-level enforcement then covers tier-narrowed cases as a best-effort backstop.
- [P2] [anthropic-fable-cli] coordinator/engine.py calls _apply_preflight_config directly at engine.py:1431 and :1861 but is not in any step's file list. If Step 5 changes _apply_preflight_config's signature to accept availability answers, those callers break.
  Suggestion: Resolve availability inside _apply_preflight_config (or give the new parameter a default) so engine.py call sites need no change, or add engine.py to Step 5's files.
- [P2] [anthropic-fable-cli] Step 1 proposes moving/sharing _availability_target/_availability_targets out of cli/check_config.py; check_config.py builds targets from ForgeConfig including reviewer/fallback keys (lines 431-556), and a move must keep the check-config CLI path working.
  Suggestion: Relocate the target-construction helpers to config/auth.py (beside ModelAvailabilityTarget) and have check_config.py import them, rather than importing CLI module code from assignment.

plan_finding_registry.description: The plan's first stated risk is carried on an acceptance-critical surface. _apply_preflight_config() derives tier-specific planner/dev/reviewer pools only after paid preflight, while sprint/runner.py can spend on _run_intake_remediation_pass() before run_batch_preflight(). Step 4 promises only an 'earliest possible' precheck followed by exact enforcement after assignment, which explicitly permits preflight or intake spend before discovering that the actual phase pool is empty. The generic zero-spend test in Step 7 does not enumerate tier-dependent exhaustion or intake-remediation spend.

Steps 4 and 5 do not account for all callers of _apply_preflight_config(). Besides coordinator/preflight_flow.py, it is called directly from coordinator/engine.py on cache-valid fresh and resume paths. Sprint execution normally obtains batch-preflight state through sprint/collision.py::run_batch_preflight() and later enters those cached paths. Without updating engine.py, a new routing-refusal exception can escape as a generic failure, and later stories can reuse routing resolved during the upfront batch rather than resolving current availability at their actual selection boundary.

Risk 1 (spend ordering) is retired only partially. Step 4 says catch the refusal 'at the coordinator routing boundary and at sprint pre-dispatch where possible' — but by the time assign_models runs, preflight complexity has already been paid, so a refusal raised only there would violate the AC's 'before any spend on that story'. Step 7 asserts zero spend but the plan does not state where the tier-independent precheck lives.

Risk 2 (account/auth-mode-scoped availability vs identity-scoped capability exclusions) is retired in shape but the key mapping is unspecified. resolve_model_availability keys its result dict on target.key or target.canonical_id (config/auth.py:~567), while candidate pools and capability_excluded are keyed on AgentDef.name (assignment.py:2101, 2189).

Step 5's per-story resolution can trigger a live account-catalog fetch (_openai_catalog) on every story; the resolver only memoizes catalogs within a single call, so failure/latency behavior across stories is unspecified.

Plan risk 1 (preflight complexity is itself paid spend) is retired for the whole-phase-empty case by the Step 4 pre-dispatch precheck and Step 7's zero-spend test, but one residual is unaddressed: if tier/exploration selection after paid preflight narrows the pool in a way that only then empties it (e.g. tier-pinned profiles), some preflight spend precedes the stop. The AC reads 'before any spend on that story'.

coordinator/engine.py calls _apply_preflight_config directly at engine.py:1431 and :1861 but is not in any step's file list. If Step 5 changes _apply_preflight_config's signature to accept availability answers, those callers break.

finding_registry.description: When an explicit review_pool or plan_agent_review pool has an available first reviewer and an unavailable later reviewer, the later unavailable reviewer is spliced back into the runtime reviewer list and the reconciled routing decision marks it included.
When two candidates in the same phase share the same model string and both catalog answers are unavailable, check_sprint_availability collapses them to one excluded entry and returns no stop.
After one run warns that a model is unverified, a later run in the same Python process using the same model and state emits no unverified warning.

On the live coordinator path the preflight agent runs and is charged (preflight_flow.py:534) before availability is resolved and routing is applied (preflight_flow.py:1140), so a NoAvailableModelError raised there stops the story after preflight spend while its operator-facing message asserts 'Nothing dispatched, $0.00 spent'.

When a role pool empties from the combination of capability exclusions and availability exclusions, the whole-pool guard raises NoAvailableModelError naming only the availability-excluded agents, so the stop message can attribute the emptiness entirely to account availability while capability records removed the other candidates.

check_sprint_availability keys its excluded map by model name while phase_keys is per profile, so a phase whose candidate list contains two profiles with the same model name never satisfies len(excluded) == len(phase_keys) and the launch gate silently passes even when every candidate is unavailable, deferring the stop to the router.

AVAILABILITY_WARNINGS is a process-wide singleton with a reset() method that no production code calls, so in a process that runs more than one sprint the 'once per run' warning is actually once per process and a later sprint's unverified models are silently unannounced.

When availability changes after sprint launch and leaves a later story unroutable, the story invokes and records its cost-bearing preflight agent before reading the fresh availability answer, so the reported $0.00 routing stop can occur after spend.
A per-story RoutingStopped result is classified as FAILED and does not set the sprint stop condition, so the routing outcome marks the story failed while independent stories remain schedulable.
With assignment disabled, story configuration returns before availability resolution, so static runs emit no unverified warning and ignore model-access changes after sprint launch.

When the post-plan availability answer marks the already-seated dev model unavailable, checkpoint bypasses or the absence of a reduced-tier replacement preserve that model for the subsequent DEV dispatch.
When availability excludes one candidate and a capability rule excludes the other, the empty-pool refusal names only the availability-excluded candidate and omits the other model and its reason.

soft: Coordinator is pure Python — no LLM calls for routing or process decisions
Schema validation is the integrity boundary — do not relax cross-validation rules

Keep modules single-purpose. Extract when a responsibility separates from its neighbours — never to satisfy a line count. Putting a change in an already-large module is correct if that is where it belongs; a module carved at whatever line got the count down is worse than the large module it came from.
Keep pure-data types in low-dependency modules with stdlib-only imports
Separate prompt construction, output parsing, and coordinator control flow

When adding or modifying data that flows between coordinator phases, instrument the change so the actual values are visible in the audit trail — diagnosing sprint failures requires tracing real data, not reconstructing it
Do not create files outside src/, tests/, or docs/. If you need a scratch file for exploration, delete it before committing.

Changes that affect coordinator phase boundaries, state handoff between phases, or adaptive routing/config propagation must include seam-level integration tests covering the touched boundary. Unit tests alone are insufficient when correctness depends on cross-phase state flow.

plan_structured.approach: Keep availability as a fresh, pure routing input: resolve account-catalog answers at story/selection boundaries, pass those answers into assignment, and treat only unavailable as a hard exclusion. Surface routing stops as scheduler/coordinator routing outcomes with zero model history mutation, while leaving unverified candidates ordered exactly as today.

steps.description: Add reusable availability target and exclusion helpers
steps.details: Reuse the existing ModelAvailabilityTarget, resolve_model_availability, and check-config _availability_target/_availability_targets logic by moving or sharing target construction so assignment/coordinator code can resolve AgentDef and ModelProfile dispatch identities without duplicating CLI-only helpers. Add a canonical assignment exclusion reason such as model_unavailable to EXCLUSION_REASONS, plus a detail builder that records state, auth_mode, checked_at, freshness, and provider reason without logging secrets.

steps.description: Filter unavailable models inside assignment candidate selection
steps.details: Extend assign_models' existing optional pure-input pattern used by capability_records with current availability answers. Apply the availability filter before _pick_agent, _select_reviewers, dev exploration, explicit pins, fallback selection, and _enforce_budget role_pools so no unavailable agent can be seated by any fallback path. Record availability exclusions in RoutingEvidence and render them in _single_model_pool and _reviewer_candidate_pool using the same candidate_pool entry shape as capability_excluded/self-review entries.

steps.description: Preserve unverified eligibility and emit one warning per model
steps.details: Treat MODEL_AVAILABILITY_UNVERIFIED as included for all routing and reranking paths, with no score, tier, reliability, value, or cost-order changes. Add a sprint/coordinator warning tracker so each canonical model identity with an unverified answer logs a single ROUTING warning per run, while repeated stories using the same model do not repeat the warning.

steps.description: Stop cleanly when availability empties a phase pool
steps.details: Add an availability-specific routing refusal parallel to NoCapableCandidateError, carrying role/phase and every excluded model with canonical detail. Catch it at the coordinator routing boundary and at sprint pre-dispatch where possible, record a routing_no_available_model outcome as skipped/routing-stopped rather than agent failure, set cost_usd to 0.0 for undispatched stories, and do not call model_profiles_storage or model_capabilities writers from this path.

steps.description: Resolve availability fresh at each selection boundary
steps.details: Call resolve_model_availability immediately before each story's routing/preflight decision rather than at sprint startup. Pass fresh answers into _apply_preflight_config/assign_models and into plan_flow's apply_post_plan_checkpoint path so later stories, and post-plan reroutes, see changed account-catalog answers without restarting.

Teach render_routing_decision and live/status displays to render model_unavailable details as 'not available to this account under <auth_mode> (checked <timestamp>)' and routing_no_available_model stops as ROUTING outcomes, matching the existing candidate-pool exclusion presentation.

Cover unavailable exclusion in every phase candidate_pool, exact canonical detail fields, unverified routing parity with a baseline decision, one-time unverified warnings, routing refusal with all excluded reasons and zero spend, no capability-history/model-profile writes on refusal, and fresh per-story availability by making consecutive resolver calls return different answers.

criteria_mapping.criterion: A model resolved unavailable appears in no phase's candidate pool. Its exclusion is recorded in the routing decision with a canonical reason naming the auth mode and the time of the availability answer, in the same place and shape other exclusions (self-review, taint) are recorded today.

A model resolved unverified remains fully eligible, and the run warns exactly once per model that its availability is unconfirmed. Routing among unverified models is identical to routing today; nothing degrades for a provider that publishes no catalog.

A phase left with no available or unverified model stops the run before any spend on that story, naming every excluded model and its reason. The stop is a routing outcome, not an agent failure, and is never recorded against any model's capability history.
Exclusion is applied at the moment of selection from the current availability answer, so an answer that changes between stories in one sprint changes routing for later stories without a restart.

risks.description: The spec says before any spend on that story, but exact dev/planner tier selection depends on preflight complexity, which itself is normally paid.
risks.mitigation: Add the earliest possible sprint/coordinator availability precheck before dispatch, then enforce the exact phase pool immediately at assignment so no plan/dev/review spend occurs after a phase is known empty.

risks.description: Availability is account/auth-mode specific while existing capability exclusions are identity/capability specific.
risks.mitigation: Keep the candidate_pool shape stable but put auth_mode, checked_at, freshness, and provider reason in the entry detail dict so machine-readable reason codes stay canonical.
